notYet: Not yet part of the Mediterranean

stages.name: Roman allies & clients
stages.desc: Kingdoms and cities outside Roman rule, bound to Rome by treaty or friendship

stages.name: Roman provinces
stages.desc: Italy and the lands ruled directly by Roman governors

stages.name: Seleucid lands
stages.desc: The shrinking kingdom of the Seleucids, ruled from Antioch

stages.name: Ptolemaic lands
stages.desc: The Ptolemaic kingdom of Egypt and Cyprus

stages.name: Free Phoenician cities
stages.desc: Tyre, Sidon and their neighbours, self-governing after Seleucid rule

stages.name: Pirate bases
stages.desc: Coasts where the pirate fleets held sway, beyond any state's control

stages.name: Pontic conquests
stages.desc: Lands taken by Mithridates VI of Pontus or by his ally Tigranes of Armenia

states.name: Cyprus
timeline: Ptolemaic Cyprus, a base for Egypt's fleet and its copper trade

states.name: Israel
timeline: Seleucid coast and Galilee
John Hyrcanus expands the independent Hasmonean state, an ally of Rome

states.name: Palestine
timeline: Seleucid Judaea; the Maccabean revolt begins
Judaea under Simon is freed of Seleucid tribute, with a Roman treaty of friendship

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Phoenician Tyre, Sidon and Berytus under Seleucid rule
Tyre wins its freedom; Sidon follows in 111
Tigranes of Armenia overruns Syria; the Phoenician cities keep their own governments

states.name: Syria
timeline: The heart of the Seleucid kingdom, around Antioch and Apamea
Diodotus Tryphon seizes the throne; dynastic war tears the kingdom apart
Tigranes the Great, Mithridates' son-in-law, annexes Seleucid Syria
After Tigranocerta, Lucullus lets Antiochus XIII return to Antioch

states.name: Turkey
timeline: Pergamon, Bithynia, Cappadocia and Pontus: kingdoms friendly to Rome; Rhodes loses its mainland
Attalus III's bequest becomes the Roman province of Asia
Mithridates overruns Asia and orders the killing of its Italians
Peace of Dardanus: Mithridates gives up his conquests; Sulla fines Asia
While Lucullus fights in Armenia, Cilician pirate fleets rule the southern coast and the sea (shown for all of Turkey)
Pompey takes the pirates' surrender at Coracesium and resettles them inland

states.name: Tunisia
timeline: Carthage, bound to Rome by the treaty of 201 BC, trades again as a Phoenician city
Carthage is destroyed; its land becomes the Roman province of Africa

states.name: Greece
timeline: After Pydna, Macedon is split into four republics; Athens receives Delos from Rome
Macedonia is a Roman province; Corinth is sacked and Greece answers to its governor
Athens joins Mithridates; his general Archelaus takes Delos and much of Greece
Sulla storms Athens and defeats Archelaus at Chaeronea
Pirates sack Delos again; Metellus begins the conquest of pirate-ridden Crete

states.name: Italy
timeline: Roman Italy: Rome and its Italian allies, enriched by the conquest of Macedon
Slave estates spread across southern Italy and Sicily; Eunus leads the first Sicilian slave war
The Social War: Rome's Italian allies revolt and win citizenship
Spartacus breaks out of a gladiator school at Capua
Pirates raid Ostia, the harbour of Rome itself

states.name: Bulgaria
timeline: Thracian kingdoms; Rome befriends the Odrysian king Cotys after Pydna
Thracian tribes join Mithridates, whose armies march through Thrace
Marcus Lucullus subdues the Bessi and takes the Black Sea Greek cities

states.name: Egypt
timeline: Ptolemaic Egypt, saved from Antiochus IV by a Roman ultimatum in 168
Rome's ally Ptolemy XII Auletes takes the throne in Alexandria

events.title: Delos a free port
events.text: Rome gives Delos to Athens and makes it a duty-free port; the Delians are expelled to Achaea.

events.title: Epirus enslaved
events.text: Aemilius Paullus sacks seventy towns in Epirus; ancient writers say 150,000 people were sold.

events.title: Maccabean revolt
events.text: In Modiin, the priest Mattathias rises against Antiochus IV's ban on Jewish worship.

events.title: Rhodes impoverished
events.text: Rhodian envoys say harbour dues have fallen from a million drachmas to 150,000 a year.

events.title: Tyrian guild
events.text: Tyrian merchants and shippers on Delos, devotees of Heracles-Melqart, honour a benefactor.

events.title: Third Punic War
events.text: A Roman army lands at Utica and lays siege to Carthage.

events.title: Carthage destroyed
events.text: Scipio Aemilianus storms Carthage; the survivors, about fifty thousand, are sold.

events.title: Corinth sacked
events.text: The consul Mummius destroys Corinth; its merchants move to Delos.

events.title: Tryphon's pirates
events.text: The Seleucid usurper Diodotus Tryphon makes Coracesium a base for raiding fleets.

events.title: Judaea freed
events.text: Simon the Hasmonean wins exemption from Seleucid tribute.

events.title: Eunus' revolt
events.text: A Syrian slave, Eunus, leads the first great slave war in Sicily from Enna.

events.title: Pergamon bequeathed
events.text: King Attalus III leaves his kingdom to the Roman people.

events.title: Province of Asia
events.text: After Aristonicus' revolt, Rome organises Pergamon's lands as the province of Asia.

events.title: Seleucids fracture
events.text: Antiochus VII dies fighting Parthia; rival kings split what is left.

events.title: Tyre goes free
events.text: Tyre becomes autonomous and starts a new civic era.

events.title: Berytian clubhouse
events.text: Merchants, shippers and warehousemen of Berytus build a clubhouse and an altar to Roma on Delos.

events.title: Gracchus' tax law
events.text: Gaius Gracchus hands the taxes of Asia to Roman contractors, the publicani.

events.title: Sidon goes free
events.text: Sidon wins autonomy from the Seleucid kings.

events.title: Agora of the Italians
events.text: Italian traders build Delos' largest courtyard, perhaps a slave market.

events.title: Nicomedes' complaint
events.text: Bithynia's king says Roman tax farmers have enslaved his men; the Senate orders allied slaves freed.

events.title: Second slave war
events.text: Slaves rise again in Sicily under Salvius and Athenion.

events.title: Antonius vs pirates
events.text: The praetor Marcus Antonius campaigns against the pirates of Cilicia and Pamphylia.

events.title: Piracy law
events.text: A Roman law, inscribed at Delphi and Cnidus, orders allies to keep pirates from their ports.

events.title: Social War
events.text: Italian allies revolt at Asculum; Rome wins the war by granting citizenship.

events.title: Asian Vespers
events.text: Mithridates orders every Italian in Asia killed; ancient tolls of 80,000 or 150,000 are disputed.

events.title: Athens defects
events.text: Athens, led by the philosopher Athenion, joins Mithridates.

events.title: Delos massacre
events.text: Archelaus' forces take Delos; Appian says 20,000 died there and nearby, most of them Italians.

events.title: Sulla takes Athens
events.text: After a long siege, Sulla's legions storm Athens and the Piraeus.

events.title: Chaeronea
events.text: Sulla routs Archelaus' army in Boeotia.

events.title: Peace of Dardanus
events.text: Mithridates gives up Asia and Greece and pays an indemnity.

events.title: Asia fined
events.text: Sulla imposes twenty thousand talents on the cities of Asia, ruining many.

events.title: Tigranes in Syria
events.text: Tigranes of Armenia takes Antioch and ends Seleucid rule for fourteen years.

events.title: Servilius' campaign
events.text: Publius Servilius attacks pirate strongholds in Lycia and Isauria.

events.title: Caesar captured
events.text: Pirates seize young Julius Caesar near Pharmacusa and hold him for ransom.

events.title: Spartacus
events.text: Gladiators break out at Capua; the revolt lasts until 71.

events.title: Thracian coast taken
events.text: Marcus Lucullus captures Apollonia and the Black Sea Greek cities.

events.title: Antonius beaten off Crete
events.text: The Cretans and their pirate allies defeat Marcus Antonius' fleet.

events.title: Tigranocerta
events.text: Lucullus defeats Tigranes outside his new capital.

events.title: Delos sacked again
events.text: The pirate Athenodorus sacks Delos and enslaves its people; the legate Triarius then walls it.

events.title: Ostia raided
events.text: Pirates burn a consular fleet in Ostia, Rome's own harbour.

events.title: Gabinian law
events.text: Rome gives Pompey command of the whole sea and its coasts.

events.title: Coracesium
events.text: Pompey's fleets corner the Cilicians, who surrender their strongholds.

events.title: Pompeiopolis
events.text: Pompey settles surrendered pirates as farmers at Soli, renamed Pompeiopolis.

chartNote: Share of the area of eleven present-day countries, by the power that dominated most of each. Regions are today's boundaries, a simplification: Turkey, Greece and Syria were divided among several powers at once, and the Cilician pirate coast of 69–67 BC is shown for all of Turkey. Dates mark turning points; ancient figures for slaves and the dead are uncertain.
